content: 1. On April 2, 2021, a report titled Prevailing Against Pandemics by Putting People at the Centre was published in relation to World AIDS Day. This document was accessed on May 17, 2021. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released interim guidance on June 1, 2020, titled Maintaining Essential Health Services: Operational Guidance for the COVID-19 Context. This document was accessed on June 29, 2021. 3. The second edition of the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development was made available and accessed on June 29, 2021. 4. Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Kunz R, Falck-Ytter Y, Vist GE, Liberati A, and colleagues published an article in 2008 in the BMJ titled Going from Evidence to Recommendations, which discusses the process of translating evidence into actionable recommendations. 5. Kravchenko N, Denisiuk O, Kuznetsova J, Jayaraj J, Zachariah R, and Smyrnov P conducted a study in Ukraine on engaging people who inject drugs and their peers in HIV testing and harm reduction. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in Developing Countries in 2019. 6. Mulubwa C, Hensen B, Phiri MM, Shanaube K, Schaap AJ, Floyd S, and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Zambia to evaluate the community-based distribution of oral HIV self-testing kits. Their findings were published in The Lancet in 2019. 7. Abou-Saleh MT, Rice P, and Foley S explored the use of dried blood spot testing for hepatitis C among drug users and the uptake of an innovative self-administered dried blood spot test. Their study was published in Addiction Disorders and Their Treatment in 2013. 8. Canfield S, Samuel MI, Ritchie D, McDonald C, Brady M, and Taylor C investigated the use and acceptability of salivary hepatitis C virus testing in an English Young Offender Institution. Their findings were published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2017. 9. Guise A, Witzel TC, Mandal S, Sabin C, Rhodes T, Nardone A, and colleagues conducted a qualitative assessment of the acceptability of hepatitis C remote self-testing and self-sampling among people who use drugs in London, UK. Their study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2018. 10. Prinsenberg T, Rebers S, Boyd A, Zuure F, Prins M, van der Valk M, and colleagues demonstrated the feasibility of dried blood spot self-sampling at home for hepatitis C RNA detection. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2020. 11. Majam M, Fischer A, Reipold EI, Rhagnath N, Msolomba V, and Lalla-Edward ST conducted a lay-user assessment of the usability and interpretation of a hepatitis C virus self-testing device in Johannesburg, South Africa. Their study was published in Diagnostics in 2021. 12. Figueroa C, Johnson C, Verster A, and Baggaley R reviewed attitudes and acceptability of HIV self-testing among key populations. Their literature review was published in AIDS Behavior in 2015. 13. Brouard C, Saboni L, Gautier A, Chevaliez S, Rahib D, Richard J-B, and colleagues assessed hepatitis C and hepatitis B prevalence using home blood self-sampling and screening history in the general population in 2016. Their findings contributed to the new French screening strategy and were published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2019. 14. Jamil LH, Duffy MC, Fakhouri M, and Jamiil HJ studied the prevalence of antibodies to the hepatitis C virus among Arab and Chaldean Americans in southeast Michigan, USA. Their findings were published in Ethnicity & Disease in 2013. 15. Kimble MM, Stafylis C, Treut P, Saab S, and Klausner JD conducted a clinical evaluation of a hepatitis C antibody rapid immunoassay using self-collected oral fluid specimens. Their study was published in Diagnostic Microbiology and Infectious Disease in 2019. 16. O’Brien JM, Kruzel KE, Wandell MG, Vinogradov IV, Sheagren JN, and Frank AP evaluated the detection of hepatitis C antibodies using at-home collection kits and an innovative laboratory algorithm. Their findings were published in Infectious Disease Clinical Practice in 2001. 17. Quoilin S, Hutse V, Vandenberghe H, Claeys F, Verhaegen E, De Cock L, and colleagues conducted a population-based prevalence study of hepatitis A, B, and C viruses using oral fluid in Flanders, Belgium. Their study was published in the European Journal of Epidemiology in 2007. 18. Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Vist GE, Kunz R, Falck-Ytter Y, Alonso-Coello P, and colleagues introduced the GRADE system, which provides a consensus on rating the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations. Their work was published in the BMJ in 2008. 19. The WHO outlined a collaborative procedure for accelerated registration of medicines, which was accessed on May 15, 2021. 20. Kumwenda MK, Johnson CC, Choko AT, Lora W, Sibande W, Sakala D, and colleagues explored social harms during the distribution of HIV self-testing kits in Malawi using mixed-methods approaches. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 21. Sibanda E, Neuman M, Tumushime M, Hatzold K, Watadzaushe C, Mutseta M, and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Zimbabwe to evaluate linkage to care after HIV self-testing. Their findings were presented at the Conference on Opportunistic Infections and Retroviruses in 2018. 22. MacPherson P, Lalloo DG, Webb EL, Maheswaran H, Choko AT, Makombe SD, and colleagues studied the effect of optional home initiation of HIV care following HIV self-testing on antiretroviral therapy initiation among adults in Malawi. Their randomized clinical trial was published in JAMA in 2014. 23. Nichols B, Cele R, Chasela C, Siwale Z, Lungu A, and Long L evaluated the cost and impact of community-based, assisted HIV self-testing among youth in Zambia. Their findings were presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in 2019. 24. Tahlil KM, Ong JJ, Rosenberg NE, Tang W, Conserve DF, Nkengasong S, and colleagues conducted a global systematic review to verify the use and results of HIV self-testing. Their findings were published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2020.
